projects.title: Machine Learning for Antimicrobial Resistance Prediction
projects.description: Codeveloped CARE: a causal machine learning framework to estimate how different antibiotic treatments affect the development of resistance under supervision of Harvard MD. Utilized Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation (TMLE) and inverse probability weighting to obtain robust causal estimates related to resistance patterns.

activity.title: AutoAce (YC F25) is building the AI-native operating system for car dealerships, starting with voice agents that automate customer communication and operations across service, sales, parts, and F&I. Dealerships lose up to 40% of inbound calls as staff juggle phones, walk-ins, and status updates. This chaos costs millions in lost revenue and burns out employees. AutoAce gives every department an AI assistant that answers calls 24/7, books appointments, sends updates, and provides real-time visibility through transcripts and analytics. The founders, Bradley Bunch and Michael Wong , are recent MIT grads who skipped class to shadow and work at car dealerships. They saw the pain firsthand and started coding inside the stores to fix it. They're already live and driving six-figure monthly revenue gains for dealerships. The future of dealership operations runs on AI. Congrats on the launch, Bradley and Michael! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/gFUfWqSH

What an incredible event! 🎤 The 6th U.S. Universities Arabic Debating Championship was a huge success, bringing together over 160 participants from universities all across the United States. It was so inspiring to see the talent and passion for debate and the Arabic language on full display. Huge congratulations to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology team for taking home the championship title! A big shout-out to the Stanford University team for a strong second-place finish, and to the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill team for winning Best Non-Native Arabic-Speaking Team. Proud to see the power of dialogue in action! #QatarDebate | #USADC

Excited to share that Sciloop (YC F25) is now backed by Y Combinator in the F25 batch. I met my cofounder Osman Siddique 3 years ago when we were representing Pakistan at International Physics Olympiad 2022. Back then, Massachusetts Institute of Technology was a far fetched dream. If there were 1000 doors leading to 1000 different futures, only one of them would have led to MIT. In that moment, if you had told me that it would be two of us attending MIT together, I would have just laughed at you. YC is just the beginning of a really long, and perhaps a really tough journey. But I'm happy to have Osman by my side. Thank you to the admission officers at MIT who saw something in my application while I got rejected from every other college in the U.S. Thank you to all the people I met at MIT, who made me grow in ways I did not even expect to. Thank you Aaron Epstein for giving us this chance, we are really excited to work with you! P.S. Found some old photos of me, Osman, and our dear friend Saaim Ahmed — takes me right back.
